description: We’re a team of developers and creators building an interactive storytelling experience around NASA’s abandoned and retired equipment on the Moon and Mars. We want to turn mission data, images, and scientific history into an engaging digital journey where users can explore these artifacts, discover their stories, and interact with an AI-powered knowledge assistant.
summary:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an immersive, interactive 3D space museum that brings the story of human-made spacecraft and exploration vehicles left on the Moon and Mars back to life.

Instead of presenting mission history through static articles, the project invites visitors on a guided cinematic journey through six real artifacts: the Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage, Surveyor 3, the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity.

Visitors explore realistic 3D environments, discover each artifact through five guided storytelling chapters, and listen to narrated explanations. An AI-powered research assistant also allows visitors to ask questions and explore verified mission information beyond the guided tour.

Our goal is to transform forgotten pieces of space exploration history into an engaging educational experience, helping people understand the technology, achievements, and scientific legacy behind humanity's journeys beyond Earth.
details:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is designed as a guided, cinematic museum experience that allows users to explore the legacy of human space exploration through the actual hardware that remains on the Moon and Mars.

How It Works

The experience begins with an immersive introduction, where visitors choose between exploring the Moon or Mars. They then enter a 3D environment and select a spacecraft or rover to begin their journey.

Each artifact is presented through five storytelling chapters:

  1. The Mission – Why the mission was launched and what it aimed to accomplish.
  2. The Machine – The engineering, design, and technology behind the vehicle.
  3. The Journey – The mission's journey, major events, and challenges.
  4. The Discoveries – Its scientific contributions and most important achievements.
  5. What Remains – What is still there today and why the artifact matters.

The experience combines interactive 3D models, cinematic camera movements, atmospheric environments, and narrated storytelling to make the exploration feel engaging and memorable. Visitors can listen to the narration while following the written content, with the ability to pause, resume, replay, or skip it.

An integrated AI assistant, Ask the Archive, gives visitors the freedom to ask additional questions about the missions and artifacts. It uses a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach to retrieve relevant information from a curated knowledge base of trusted research sources, helping keep its responses grounded in documented facts.

Technologies and Tools

The project brings together several technologies:

  • JavaScript and Three.js: Building immersive 3D environments, rendering spacecraft models, and creating interactive cinematic experiences.
  • Python and Django REST Framework: Powering the backend APIs and serving mission information.
  • Google Gemini API: Supporting the AI-powered research assistant.
  • RAG and Embeddings: Retrieving relevant information from the project's curated research material before generating answers.
  • Web Speech API: Providing browser-based narration and speech controls.
  • NASA Mission Resources and 3D Assets: Supporting the historical and scientific accuracy of the experience.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes this project different is its approach to storytelling. Rather than treating these spacecraft and rovers as obsolete equipment or presenting them as entries in a database, we transform them into the central characters of an interactive historical journey.

The experience connects real engineering achievements with their scientific discoveries and their present-day legacy. The combination of cinematic 3D exploration, structured narration, and an AI research assistant creates multiple ways for visitors to engage with the same scientific story.

Intended Impact

We want to make space exploration history more accessible, engaging, and memorable, especially for students and people who are curious about science and technology.

These artifacts represent milestones in humanity's exploration of other worlds. By bringing their stories together in one interactive experience, we hope to preserve their legacy, inspire curiosity about planetary exploration, and remind visitors that even when a mission ends, its contribution to human knowledge remains.

Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, source reliability, accessibility of information, performance in modern web browsers, and the balance between visual immersion and educational value.
